etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English avisen (“to perceive, consider, inform”), from Old French aviser, from avis, or from Late Latin advisō, from ad + visō, from Latin videō (“to see”), visum (“past participle of videō”). See also advice.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To give advice to; to offer an opinion to, as worthy or expedient to be followed.

quote.citation: 1992, Burns, D. & Pierce, J.P., Tobacco Use in California 1990-1991, Sacramento: California Department of Health Services, →ISBN, page 88:
quote.text: Of those current smokers who had seen a physician within the last year, 35.7% of the males and 27.6% of the females reported never having been advised to stop smoking by their physician.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To recommend; to offer as advice.
(transitive) To give information or notice to; to inform or counsel; — with of before the thing communicated.

quote.citation: 1843, Thomas Carlyle, “8, The Election”, in Past and Present, book 2:
quote.text: […]  Samson is reported to the King accordingly. His Majesty, advising of it for a moment, orders that Samson be brought in with the other Twelve.

definitions.definition: (obsolete, transitive) To look at, watch; to see.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book III, Canto V”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: when that villain he auiz'd, which late / Affrighted had the fairest Florimell, / Full of fiers fury, and indignant hate, / To him he turned  […]

quote.citation: 1746, Charles Pinot Duclos, The history of Lewis xi. king of France. Transl, page 169:
quote.text: The armies drawing constantly nearer to each other, the king advised with his council, whether he should march against the Britons, or sall upon the count of Gharolois.

definitions.definition: (Scots law) To deliver judgment after a case has been reserved for further consideration.
